description.narrative:
Organisationen Veritas har ansökt till ambassaden om ett kärnstöd på 9 miljoner SEK för att kunna fortsätta bedriva sin verksamhet i Zimbabwe mellan aug 2018 och aug 2021.
Insatsen ämnar att bidra till en mer öppen stat, bättre lagar, ett mer opartiskt rättssystem, ökad respekt för mänskliga rättigheter samt etablerandet av en konstitutionell demokrati. Veritas arbetar även för kvinnor och minoriteters rättighter samt att motarbeta våld och främja fred och tolerans. Aktiviteter innefattar informationsspridning, bevakning och förespråksarbete. Organisationen kommer inte ingå avtal med några andra parter men arbetar nära med relevanta aktörer för att stärka sitt inflytande på parlamentet.
Veritas totala budget för 2018 omfattar 606 382 USD av vilka TRACE (USD 126 400), Omidyar Network (USD 64 900), National Endowment for Democracy (NED) (USD 54 800) och Switzerland (USD 20 500) bidrar till. Veritas har inga enga inkomstkällor och Sverige kommer troligen vara den största givaren under avtalsperioden.

Veritas has applied to Sida for funding of 9million SEK to carry out project titled "Working for Open Government, Democracy, Constitutionalism, Rule of Law, Justice and Human Rights" in Zimbabwe during the period 2018-2021.
The intervention is expected to contribute to a more open government, the establishment of a constitutional democracy, better laws, more impartial justice delivery and the observance of human rights. It is also expected to have a positive impact on gender equality and the inclusion of minorities, encourage greater social cohesion with a fairer distribution of wealth, greater access to social services, an end to impunity and to promote peace and tolerance over violence.
The intervention’s total budget is 606 382USD, which is contributed by TRACE (USD 126 400), Omidyar Network (USD 64 900), National Endowment for Democracy (NED) (USD 54 800) och Switzerland (USD 20 500)

The intervention is expected to contribute to a more open government, establishment of a constitutional democracy, better laws, more impartial justice delivery and the observance of human rights. It is also expected to have a positive impact on gender equality and the inclusion of minorities, encourage greater social cohesion with a fairer distribution of wealth, greater access to social services, an end to impunity and to promote peace and tolerance over violence.

The results being summarized are detailed in the final report by Veritas, titled "Working for Open Government, Constitutionalism, Rule of Law, Justice, and Human Rights," covering the period from January 2021 to August 2023.
Throughout the program period, Veritas has successfully enhanced its valuable information service, focusing on the activities of Parliament. The organization has conducted thorough analyses of Bills, Acts, and statutory instruments to assess their constitutionality and effectiveness, while also making digital copies of legislation accessible to the public. This service has been utilized by legal professionals, parliamentarians, and the general public, with many lawyers considering it an indispensable resource for their practice. The information provided has been further amplified through extensive use of social media. Veritas has also delivered comprehensive education to the public regarding the various avenues for engaging with Parliament and submitting feedback. They have effectively streamlined the processes involved to promote meaningful participation from the public.
Veritas consistently closed the information gap by availing important resources and documents such as new legislation, Bills, government documents and policies freely to the public, either in e-bulletins or on their website. The core information service and public advocacy were maintained - disseminated in its popular e-bulletins, including Bill Watch, Constitution Watch, and Court Watch, Parliamentary Committee Series which tracked legislation, monitored parliamentary committees, and reported on Constitutional Court cases. These bulletins provided all recipients with simplified summaries of key legislation and speeches in parliament, and simplified analysis from Veritas legal experts. The Veritas mailing list currently has over 10 000 active subscribers. This has increased constitutional literacy levels, quality of civic engagement and access to information.
Veritas launched a dedicated website for women, accompanied by social media platforms, to provide accessible and straightforward legal guidance to marginalized women who struggle to comprehend the legal system and cannot afford high legal fees. In light of the recent Marriages Act, which generated considerable discussion and uncertainty, they offered simplified explanations of key provisions to help women navigate the new marriage frameworks established by the Act and understand their own positions within this legal context. Additionally, they created animations on this subject, facilitating a clearer understanding of the new legislation and alleviating uncertainty. Through these platforms, Veritas has continued to highlight women's issues and provide resources that support their rights and access to justice.
Veritas successfully urged the Government to address a significant deficiency in the legal framework, thereby safeguarding children from sexual exploitation by adults. In the case of Kawenda v Minister of Justice & Ors CCZ 3/2022, initiated by Veritas, the Constitutional Court ruled that certain provisions of the Criminal Law Code, which prohibit sexual relations between adults and young individuals, were unconstitutional as they failed to protect older minors. The Court mandated that the Government enact corrective legislation within a year; however, the Government allowed this deadline to pass without action. Consequently, these provisions became entirely ineffective, leaving children of all ages without legal protection. In response to the Government's inaction, Veritas reached out to the Attorney-General, highlighting the issue and providing a proposed Bill to address it. This Bill has since been enacted into law in 2024.
Veritas has been actively monitoring the progress of the Independent Complaints Commission Bill, which aims to establish an independent body to address public grievances regarding the security services. This matter is of particular interest to Veritas, as they previously initiated legal action to compel the government to meet its constitutional duty to establish such a Commission. Subsequently, it became necessary to pursue a court case to ensure a judicial ruling on the matter. At the request of the Attorney General, Veritas drafted a Bill to implement this initiative. Regrettably, the government modified the original Bill, resulting in a Commission that is less independent than intended. The Bill has now been enacted into law.
Veritas initiated legal proceedings in the High Court to challenge the constitutionality of the Minister of Local Government's authority, as outlined in section 314 of the Urban Councils Act, to modify or invalidate resolutions made by local authorities. In early 2023, in the case of CHRA & Ors v Minister of Local Government HH-7-2023, the Court largely granted the requested order, while stipulating that the Minister retains the ability to establish overarching policy.
